Subject: Exemption coverage for merged entities / retroactive application

Hi Sean,

Quick background: Greenbrook completed an acquisition in Q2 and we recently consolidated three legacy purchasing accounts into a single parent account (Greenbrook Distribution — Tax ID: 12-3456789). Our AP team found that some Redwood invoices charged sales tax for orders placed under the legacy accounts (GB-West, GB-South) back to April.

Can Redwood: 1) confirm whether our consolidated parent EIN can be applied retroactively to clear tax on eligible invoices, and 2) accept our signed attestation and state resale certificate for TX to cover the merged accounts?

I've attached a signed corporate attestation (pdf) and the TX resale cert. If you need a POA or notarized copy we can arrange.

Requested timeline: our finance cycle closes next Friday and we'd like to resolve any tax credits/adjustments before then.

Thanks,

Hi Lena — thanks for the details and the attachments. Quick read-through and next steps from our side: 

- We can accept a single parent EIN for exemption coverage across consolidated sub-accounts, but we need documented evidence that ties the legacy account names to the parent (signed attestation + either a POA or a copy of the acquisition agreement).
- For retroactive tax relief we need to review invoice-level line items to confirm taxable product categories and order shipping addresses (some states require ship-to match).

Grace (Finance) — can you confirm if we can issue credit memos for the affected invoices pending verification?
Karthik (Tax Ops) — please confirm whether the TX certificate attached is acceptable in our intake matrix and whether a notarized attestation is required for retroactive application.

Lena — if you can provide: 1) a short mapping list (legacy account -> customer id/old account number), 2) a signed POA or acquisition agreement excerpt, and 3) confirmation of the shipping addresses for the orders in question, we can start the validation immediately. Targeting to get an initial answer within 48 business hours.

Regards,

Sean — quick finance ops update:

- We can place the disputed invoices on billing hold (stop collections) once we have the mapping and the signed attestation.
- Credit memos for retroactive tax will require: validated resale certificate covering the ship-to state, EIN match, and a reconciliation file that ties each invoice to the legacy account number.
- Accounting will need final approval from Revenue Ops for credits > $10k. Please flag if any invoice amounts exceed that.

Karthik — please confirm acceptance criteria for the TX certificate and whether the attestation needs a notary. If not, we'll ask Greenbrook for a notarized POA as a fallback.

Grace O'Connor
Manager, Billing Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <procurement@greenbrook-distribution.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exemption coverage for merged entities / retroactive application

Hi Lena — thanks for sending the docs. Quick tax intake notes: 

- The TX resale certificate provided appears valid (state tax id and signer present). For coverage across merged accounts we need explicit linkage: either a POA or a short acquisition excerpt showing asset/account transfer. A signed corporate attestation alone is acceptable for forward coverage, but for retroactive credits many states (including TX) prefer a dated acquisition agreement or POA.
- If Greenbrook can provide a CSV with the invoice numbers and legacy account IDs, our team will run the ship-to validation against state rules and return a pass/fail for each invoice.
- If any invoices fail ship-to match, we can only apply credit where legal coverage exists; otherwise those invoices remain taxable.

Please upload the CSV/POA to the shared Drive link and I'll kick off the validation. If you prefer, I can accept the CSV by reply email.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Tax Analyst | Redwood Inference
